tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/internal-http.md <<'EOF'
# Plain HTTP for internal hosts

The project's current decision is that HTTPS is enforced everywhere, with no plaintext exception for internal hosts or internal services: plain HTTP is not permitted for internal traffic, and internal endpoints are held to the same HTTPS requirement as external ones. This decision also stands alongside the rule that certificate verification stays on in all builds, with no exception for development.
EOF

result:
I created `docs/policies/internal-http.md`. It has one paragraph saying the project's current decision is to enforce HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exception for internal hosts or services. It also notes that certificate verification stays on in all builds, which is the other standing rule on record.

I didn't mention the earlier allowance for plain HTTP on internal hosts, since it was retired. The Muninn project memory has the HTTPS decision as its newest entry.

My first attempt to write the file with a shell command failed with a parser error, so I wrote it with the file tool instead. It only worked because that write created `docs/policies/`; the shell command was the one that tried to make the directory.
